o1.biggest_strength: Every cost figure checks against the brief (£139,800 in returns, 6,076 day 3–5 tickets, 540–1,080 fewer bra returns, a £11,830–£19,770 total), and there are two bra-specific fit messages after delivery that help before a return.
o1.biggest_mistake: Message 4 says 'still on track' even when the courier has not scanned the parcel, which risks a promise we cannot keep. The 23.5% low case is never explained as an adjustment for the type of buyer who uses the quiz.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Send the day-3 update only after a courier scan, say why the fit gain is halved, and name owners and a conversion guardrail for moving the quiz.

o2.biggest_strength: Sharp, honest reasoning. It halves the fit finder gap because keen buyers self-select, it warns that Christmas will distort results, it tests the button on half of bra visitors with a conversion guardrail, and it sends the day-3 message only after a courier scan, with a warehouse check when there is none.
o2.biggest_mistake: There is no follow-up 'how's the fit' message for first-time bra buyers a few days after delivery. The 35–45% exchange share is set as a day-60 target when the portal only goes live in December.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a bra-specific fit-help message after delivery and give one total gross saving per 90 days, with a more cautious day-60 exchange target.

reason: Both get the numbers right. Number 2 thinks like an operator: it adjusts the fit gain for who uses the quiz, flags Christmas, adds owners, dates and a guardrail, and never promises a day it can't keep, so it's the plan I'd rather run.
